Synthetic. Two listings arrive on one newest check. Listing 1 is in area (details-selector's `bare-title-in-area`: a city page within an active centre's radius) and is selected. Listing 2 is details-selector's `out-of-area-not-shipped` case: its city page has no active centre in reach and its delivery types are not shipping, so the selector never calls `enqueue()` for it. The first-seen event arrives three times around the selection and the submit; the queue's own handler enqueues nothing on any of them. Only listing 1 is queued and sent; listing 2 has no queue row at all, so the selector's gate ("every new ID in area or shipped gets details", `docs/decisions.md`, Precedence, Detail selection) is what decides a paid fetch.
